findings.detail: The finite commuting endomorphism algebra is finite and complete over Lambda. Its residual local-factor idempotent lifts and gives precisely the simultaneous topologically nilpotent vectors. On an omitted factor an inverse operator preserves every Lambda-adic power, so convergence to zero forces the vector to vanish. The projector lies in the commuting algebra and hence commutes with its full commutant.

Finite generation makes operator nilpotence uniform modulo each maximal-ideal power. With finitely many variables, sufficiently high total-degree monomials vanish in that quotient, so formal series evaluate by finite truncation. Completeness and separatedness give the action and its laws. A coefficient-semilinear map agreeing on Lambda is Lambda-linear and preserves all these quotients, giving the full series intertwining without an unproved arbitrary-map continuity assumption.

The canonical summand remains projective over the exact finite ell-group algebra. Its residue group algebra is local with nilpotent augmentation ideal, so the complete finite group algebra is local and a finite projective module is free. The distinguished relations (1+Y)^{ell^a}-1 identify the exact formal quotient with the group algebra, with the asserted basis and action. This includes empty variable sets and a=0.

The norm quotient is the literal quotient by all diamond-generator differences. The commuting idempotent splits this quotient, and on each discarded local factor some relevant U-difference remains invertible unless that quotient factor vanishes; no new topologically nilpotent vectors appear. This proves exactly the original primary summand and both split maps, with polynomial intertwining.

The ordered splitting algebra is finite over B. The factor with all prescribed root differences in its radical represents the original completed splitting quotient; the possible zero factor is retained. Tensoring this idempotent needs no flatness, and the original root-intertwining maps restrict with both compositions still the exact F. Finiteness over Lambda follows from finite tensor generators. In the nonzero case the B-action image is a finite local Lambda-algebra, and its radical is the radical of m_Lambda times that image; powers of m_B therefore act through arbitrary Lambda-adic powers. This proves the required topology comparison on the finite tensor module. The zero M0 case is now stated separately.
